intro: Wet room installations have become one of the most sought-after bathroom upgrades across Pinebury, and it's easy to understand why. A properly designed wet room transforms a cramped or outdated bathroom into something genuinely luxurious — fully waterproofed, level-access, and far easier to clean than a traditional shower enclosure. But getting one right in Pinebury takes more than just ripping out an old suite. The unique mix of property types in the area, the local water characteristics, and the particular challenges of working within older structures all shape how a wet room project needs to be approached. Done properly, you're looking at a long-lasting, high-value addition to your home.
localContext: Pinebury sits within the City of Edinburgh and its housing stock reflects that — a real mix of older stone-built properties and period cottages sitting alongside more recent modern estates. That variety matters a great deal when it comes to wet room installation. In the older stone-built homes and period cottages that make up a significant portion of Pinebury's housing, floors can be uneven, joists may be shallower than in modern builds, and the walls behind older plasterwork can throw up surprises once work begins. Getting the fall on the floor right for drainage — typically around 1 in 80 — is harder when you're working with a solid stone floor or a bouncy timber sub-floor that needs reinforcing first. Pinebury is also in a moderately hard water area, which is worth bearing in mind when choosing your shower fixtures and drain covers. Limescale will build up over time on chrome and exposed metalwork, so specifying the right finishes and installing a quality shower filter can save you considerable maintenance hassle down the line.
serviceDetail: A full wet room installation in Pinebury typically follows a clear sequence of work, and understanding what's involved helps you avoid surprises. The first stage is a thorough survey of the existing bathroom — checking floor strength, existing waste pipe positions, wall construction, and whether the space has adequate ventilation. In Pinebury's older properties especially, this survey stage is non-negotiable; a floor that looks fine can have hidden rot or insufficient depth to accommodate a recessed drain without major structural work. Once the survey is complete and a design agreed, the existing bathroom is stripped back to the bare structure. The floor is then prepared — levelled if needed, reinforced where required — before a tanking system is applied. Tanking is the waterproof membrane that covers the entire floor and walls to a specified height, and it is the most critical part of the job. Skimping here leads to water ingress, damp, and eventual damage to the floor and ceiling below. After tanking, the shower drain is set, floor tiles are laid to the correct gradient, and wall tiling or panels are fitted. Finally, the shower, any screen or glass panel, heated towel rail, and sanitary ware go in. A straightforward installation in a standard Pinebury bathroom typically takes five to seven working days, though older properties with structural complications can extend that timeline.
pricing: In Pinebury, a wet room installation typically costs between £6,000 and £12,000, depending on the size of the space, the complexity of the existing structure, and the quality of fixtures and finishes you choose. A modest bathroom in a modern Pinebury estate property with straightforward access and standard-spec fittings will sit towards the lower end of that range. A period cottage with a solid stone floor, tricky waste runs, or a desire for premium tiles and a rainfall shower setup can comfortably reach the upper end. Additional costs to factor in include any required ventilation upgrades, underfloor heating if desired, and electrical work — which must be carried out by a Part P registered electrician. Always get an itemised quote rather than a single lump sum figure.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Pinebury well makes a real difference on a project like this. Someone familiar with the local housing stock understands the quirks of stone-built properties and period cottages — the kinds of things that only reveal themselves once you start opening up walls and floors. They'll also have existing relationships with local suppliers and be easier to contact if a snag needs addressing after the job is done. Wet room installations are high-value projects where the quality of the waterproofing is everything; you want someone accountable and reachable, not a travelling team who'll be three counties away by the time you notice a problem.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in one of Pinebury's older stone-built properties?
faqs.a: Yes, but it requires careful planning. Stone floors may need significant preparation or even replacement of the sub-floor to achieve the correct gradient for drainage. Walls in older Pinebury properties often need thorough assessment before tanking is applied. It's more complex than a modern build, but absolutely achievable with the right installer who understands older construction methods.

faqs.q: How does Pinebury's moderately hard water affect a wet room long-term?
faqs.a: Hard water causes limescale to build up on shower heads, drain covers, and chrome fittings over time. In a wet room — where water hits exposed surfaces constantly — this can look unsightly and block flow if left untreated. Specifying brushed or matt finishes rather than polished chrome, and fitting an inline shower filter, are both practical steps that reduce the maintenance burden considerably.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Pinebury?
faqs.a: Most wet room installations in Pinebury take between five and eight working days from strip-out to final fit-off. Modern estate properties with straightforward layouts tend to come in at the shorter end. Older stone cottages or properties requiring floor reinforcement, replumbing of waste runs, or remedial structural work will take longer — your installer should give you a realistic timeline after the initial survey.

faqs.q: Is planning permission required for a wet room in Pinebury?
faqs.a: In most cases, no — wet room installations are considered permitted development and don't require planning consent. However, if your Pinebury property is listed or sits within a conservation area, you may need to check with Edinburgh Council before structural alterations begin. Your installer should flag this during the survey stage if it applies to your property.
